audit_name: M12 Study 4 revised independent source and corpus review
verdict_scope: Source metadata, abstract support, exact excerpt text, draft scope, and source disjointness only.

all_other_differences.new: Three abstract-scope draft corrections and two exact punctuation corrections from independent audit before registration; neutrophil recommendation shortened to fit original 200-character boundary. No retrieval-performance screening.

revised_claim_reviews.basis: Abstract explicitly states ATP-bound FtsEX activates septal PG hydrolysis of EnvC-AmiB and that EnvC-AmiB alone exhibits autoinhibition.
Abstract reports constrained HMGCR function, decreased GGPP, reduced Rac1 prenylation, greater IQGAP1 binding, and NLRP3 activation; human-monocyte setting matches the source title and abstract.

Abstract states resting human peripheral-blood neutrophils rely on glycogen as a major source, switch to primarily extracellular glucose after activation through increased GLUT1, and show function-specific effects.

records.title: Structure and activity of the septal peptidoglycan hydrolysis machinery crucial for bacterial cell division.
records.draft: In E. coli, ATP-bound FtsEX activates septal peptidoglycan hydrolysis by EnvC-AmiB; EnvC-AmiB alone is autoinhibited.

records.title: Metabolic regulator LKB1 controls adipose tissue ILC2 PD-1 expression and mitochondrial homeostasis to prevent insulin resistance.
records.draft: Adipose ILC2 LKB1 loss activates NFAT-dependent PD-1, heightening mitophagy and worsening obesity-linked insulin resistance.

records.title: Astrocyte-secreted neurocan controls inhibitory synapse formation and function.
records.draft: Astrocyte-derived neurocan is cleaved, and its C-terminal domain localizes to somatostatin-positive synapses to promote cortical inhibitory synapse formation.

records.title: Protist predation promotes antimicrobial resistance spread through antagonistic microbiome interactions.
records.draft: Soil protist predation can spread antibiotic resistance by favoring bacteria that release antagonistic metabolites, which in turn support resistant bacteria.

records.title: A host-microbiota interactome reveals extensive transkingdom connectivity.
records.draft: Human-associated bacterial strains show tissue-specific exoprotein binding; distinct strain profiles correspond to different host-cell and immune effects.

records.title: p20BAP31 promotes cell apoptosis via interaction with GRP78 and activating the PERK pathway in colorectal cancer.
records.draft: In colorectal cancer cells, p20BAP31 competitively binds GRP78 away from PERK, amplifying the unfolded-protein response and apoptosis.

records.title: Cyclo(Pro-Tyr) elicits conserved cellular damage in fungi by targeting the [H+]ATPase Pma1 in plasma membrane domains.
records.draft: Cyclo(Pro-Tyr) disrupts fungal membrane polarization; damage is associated with destabilization of Pma1-containing plasma-membrane domains.

records.title: Presynaptic sensor and silencer of peptidergic transmission reveal neuropeptides as primary transmitters in pontine fear circuit.
records.draft: In the pontine threat pathway, neuropeptides rather than glutamate encode the unconditioned stimulus during Pavlovian threat learning.

records.title: Glucose-oxygen deprivation constrains HMGCR function and Rac1 prenylation and activates the NLRP3 inflammasome in human monocytes.
records.draft: In human monocytes, glucose-oxygen deprivation constrains HMGCR function, reduces GGPP synthesis and Rac1 prenylation, increases IQGAP1 binding, and activates NLRP3.

records.title: Arabidopsis BBX14 is involved in high light acclimation and seedling development.
records.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
records.draft: In Arabidopsis seedlings, GLK1 directly targets BBX14 downstream of GUN1; BBX14 supports high-light acclimation and early chlorophyll production.

records.title: The molecular framework balancing growth and defense in response to plant elicitor peptide-induced signals in Arabidopsis.
records.draft: Following Arabidopsis PEP1 danger signaling, STZ differentially regulates root-meristem cell-cycle, differentiation, and stress-response programs.

records.title: Activation induces shift in nutrient utilization that differentially impacts cell functions in human neutrophils.
records.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
records.draft: Resting human neutrophils rely on glycogen as a major metabolic source; activation drives a GLUT1-enabled switch to primarily extracellular glucose, with function-specific effects.

Registration/freezing and any scientific or validator claims remain the coordinator’s responsibility.
